quests.instruction: Fiona and Enzo want to share one cookie. Fiona cuts it, and Enzo chooses first. Why does this plan work?
quests.correctAnswer: Fiona will cut it as evenly as she can 🍪
options: Fiona will cut it as evenly as she can 🍪
Enzo is older, so he decides 👑
Fiona cannot touch the cookie again 🚫
quests.hint: Think about what Fiona wants, knowing Enzo picks first.
quests.explanation: If you know the other person chooses first, you cut as evenly as possible, because you might get the smaller piece. Both end up with a fair share.
quests.funFact: This 'I cut, you choose' trick has been used for a very long time to divide things fairly.

quests.instruction: A tablet has to be shared by three siblings for one hour. How long does each child get if the time is split equally?
quests.correctAnswer: 20 minutes ⏱️
options: 15 minutes ⏱️
20 minutes ⏱️
30 minutes ⏱️
quests.hint: Divide 60 minutes among three children.
quests.explanation: 60 ÷ 3 = 20, so each child gets 20 minutes.
quests.funFact: People who share a computer at work often book time slots, which is the same idea as a family schedule.

quests.instruction: Three children share a bag of 12 stickers. Gael says he should get more because he is the oldest. What is the fairest reply?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Let's all get 4 stickers each.' 🌟
options: 'You can have 8, and we'll share the rest.' 🙄
'Let's all get 4 stickers each.' 🌟
'Whoever grabs them first gets them.' 🏃
quests.hint: Share equally unless there is a good reason to do something else.
quests.explanation: 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Being the oldest does not mean getting more. Sharing equally is fair when everyone has the same need.
quests.funFact: Studies show that children as young as about four notice when things are shared unfairly.

quests.instruction: Caleb wants to spend Saturday at the beach, and Lia wants to visit the museum. Which plan is a compromise?
quests.correctAnswer: Beach in the morning, museum later 🏖️
options: Beach all day long, and no museum at all 🏖️
Museum all day long, and no beach at all 🏛️
Beach in the morning, museum later 🏖️
quests.hint: A compromise gives each person some of what they want.
quests.explanation: In a compromise, each person gives up a little so that both get something. Splitting the day does exactly that.
quests.funFact: The word 'compromise' comes from a Latin word meaning a joint promise.

quests.instruction: Which of these is NOT a compromise?
quests.correctAnswer: Always getting your own way 😎
options: Taking turns choosing the movie 🎬
Meeting halfway on bedtime 🌙
Always getting your own way 😎
quests.hint: A compromise needs both people to give something.
quests.explanation: If one person always wins, nobody is compromising. A compromise means both sides adjust.
quests.funFact: In many families, small compromises happen every day, from what to eat to which show to watch.

quests.instruction: In a family vote, three people want to go to the park and two want to go to the zoo. The park wins. What is a fair way to respect the zoo group too?
quests.correctAnswer: Plan the zoo for another weekend 🦁
options: Tell them their idea was silly 🙅
Plan the zoo for another weekend 🦁
Skip both and stay home 🏠
quests.hint: A fair family remembers everyone's wishes, even when one idea wins today.
quests.explanation: A vote decides one choice, but a fair family keeps the other idea in mind, such as saving the zoo for another time.
quests.funFact: Some families keep a 'next time' list so that good ideas are not forgotten.

quests.instruction: Bryn and her brother share a bedroom. Bryn likes to read at night, but her brother goes to sleep early. What could they do?
quests.correctAnswer: Bryn reads using a small, dim light 💡
options: Bryn stops reading forever 📕
Bryn turns on the big ceiling light 🔆
Bryn reads using a small, dim light 💡
quests.hint: Find a way that lets both people do what they need.
quests.explanation: A small reading light lets Bryn read without keeping her brother awake. Good sharing meets both people's needs.
quests.funFact: Dim, warm lights are less likely to disturb sleep than bright, cool ones.

quests.instruction: Ismael and his sister share a bookshelf. How could they divide it fairly?
quests.correctAnswer: Agree who uses which shelves 📚
options: The older child takes every shelf 📚
Mix all the books and never sort them 📚
Agree who uses which shelves 📚
quests.hint: Agreeing together is better than deciding alone.
quests.explanation: Dividing space by agreement means each person knows what is theirs, which cuts down on arguments.
quests.funFact: Many shared bedrooms use colored boxes or labels so that each child knows what belongs to them.

quests.instruction: Joss's cousin is staying for a week and sleeping in Joss's room. What helps them get along?
quests.correctAnswer: Agreeing on a few simple room rules 📝
options: Pretending the cousin is not there at all 🙈
Agreeing on a few simple room rules 📝
Hiding all of his toys in the cupboard 🧸
quests.hint: Good hosts and good guests both need to know the plan.
quests.explanation: A few rules made together, like where to put bags and when to turn off the light, help two people share a room happily.
quests.funFact: Guests often feel more comfortable when they are told where things are and what the plan is.

quests.instruction: Four people share one bathroom, and everyone needs to leave at 7:30. Which plan works best?
quests.correctAnswer: Agree an order with short time slots 🕖
options: Whoever shouts loudest goes first 📢
Everyone crowds in at the same time 🚪
Agree an order with short time slots 🕖
quests.hint: A plan means everyone knows when it is their turn.
quests.explanation: An agreed order with time limits gives everyone a fair turn and helps the family leave on time.
quests.funFact: Some families stick a simple schedule on the bathroom door.

quests.instruction: It is Rowan's turn in the bathroom next, but his little sister says she really needs the toilet right now. What is a kind choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Let her go first this time 🚽
options: Tell her she must wait 10 minutes ⏳
Lock the door quickly 🔒
Let her go first this time 🚽
quests.hint: Some needs cannot wait.
quests.explanation: A need that cannot wait comes before a regular turn. Letting her go first is kind, and Rowan can have the next turn.
quests.funFact: A need cannot be put off, but a want can, and that helps when deciding who goes first.

quests.instruction: Why do some families use a shower timer?
quests.correctAnswer: So everyone gets a fair turn ♨️
options: So everyone gets a fair turn ♨️
To make every shower last longer ⏱️
To stop anyone from showering 🚿
quests.hint: Hot water and time are shared.
quests.explanation: A timer helps share limited hot water and bathroom time, and it saves water too.
quests.funFact: Using less hot water in the shower also saves energy and money.

quests.instruction: The baby is asleep, and Sia and her brother want to play. What is a good choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Play a quiet game somewhere else 🃏
options: Play a quiet game somewhere else 🃏
Play a loud drum game right there 🥁
Race around near the baby's door 🏃
quests.hint: Think of an activity that will not wake anyone.
quests.explanation: Choosing a quiet activity, or a different place, respects a sleeping baby's need for rest.
quests.funFact: Newborn babies sleep for about 14 to 17 hours a day.

quests.instruction: A grown-up is on a work call at home, and Tove wants to practice the drums. What is the best choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Play later, or use a quiet pad 🥁
options: Play at full volume right now 🥁
Play later, or use a quiet pad 🥁
Stop playing music for good 🚫
quests.hint: Find a way to keep your hobby and respect other people's work.
quests.explanation: Waiting, or using a quieter way to practice, lets Tove keep playing without disturbing the call.
quests.funFact: Practice pads make much less noise than a full drum, so many drummers use them at home.

quests.instruction: Vito wants to listen to music while his sister does her homework. What is a fair solution?
quests.correctAnswer: Use headphones so both are happy 🎧
options: Use headphones so both are happy 🎧
Play it on speakers for everyone 🔊
Make her do homework in the hall 🚶
quests.hint: Is there a way to meet both needs at the same time?
quests.explanation: Headphones let Vito enjoy his music without disturbing his sister's concentration.
quests.funFact: Keeping the volume moderate also helps protect your hearing.

quests.instruction: The TV remote is missing, and everyone is blaming each other. What helps most?
quests.correctAnswer: Calmly search the usual places together 🔍
options: Argue about who lost it for an hour 😠
Calmly search the usual places together 🔍
Decide that nobody can watch TV again 📺
quests.hint: Solving a problem together works better than blaming.
quests.explanation: Searching calmly in the usual spots, together, is faster than arguing. Blaming rarely finds a lost item.
quests.funFact: Lost things are often found close to where they were last used.

quests.instruction: The family notices the milk is nearly gone. What helps make sure it gets replaced?
quests.correctAnswer: Add it to the shopping list ✅
options: Hope somebody else will notice 🙈
Add it to the shopping list ✅
Finish it and say nothing 🥛
quests.hint: Think about a way to make sure the next shop includes it.
quests.explanation: A shared list lets everyone note what is running out so that the next trip includes it.
quests.funFact: Some families use a whiteboard or a phone list that everyone can add to.

quests.instruction: Water is dripping from under the kitchen sink. What should be done first?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a grown-up straight away 💧
options: Wait to see if it stops by itself 🕰️
Wipe it up and say nothing 🧽
Tell a grown-up straight away 💧
quests.hint: Some household problems need someone with experience.
quests.explanation: A leak can damage the home or make the floor slippery, so a grown-up should know quickly. Wiping up may help, but the leak still needs fixing.
quests.funFact: A small drip can waste hundreds of liters of water over a year.

quests.instruction: In a cooperative board game, all the players work together against the game. How does the game end?
quests.correctAnswer: Everyone wins or loses together 🤝
options: One person wins and the others lose 🏆
Everyone is out of the game 😞
Everyone wins or loses together 🤝
quests.hint: Cooperative means working together.
quests.explanation: In cooperative games, players share one goal and win or lose as a team. They talk and plan together.
quests.funFact: Cooperative board games, such as Forbidden Island, have become popular with families.

quests.instruction: Zev's little sister cannot run as fast as the others in a garden race. What can the family do so everyone enjoys it?
quests.correctAnswer: Give her a head start 🏃
options: Give her a head start 🏃
Tell her she cannot play 🚫
Wait until she is older ⏳
quests.hint: Rules can be changed so that everyone can take part.
quests.explanation: A head start or another small change helps players of different ages join the same game.
quests.funFact: In golf and some other sports, 'handicaps' are used so that players of different skill can compete fairly.

quests.instruction: After a family relay race, Wendell's team loses. What is a good sportsmanlike response?
quests.correctAnswer: Say 'well done' to the winners 👏
options: Say 'well done' to the winners 👏
Complain that the other team cheated 🚩
Refuse to ever race with them again 🙅
quests.hint: Think about how you want others to treat you when you win.
quests.explanation: Congratulating the winners and enjoying the game together is good sportsmanship.
quests.funFact: Many sports end with a handshake or high five to show respect for opponents.

quests.instruction: A family is choosing where to go on holiday. Which is the best first step?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask each person for their ideas 🗣️
options: Choose the place without asking anyone 💰
Ask each person for their ideas 🗣️
Let one person decide everything alone 👑
quests.hint: Everyone who is going has a stake in the choice.
quests.explanation: Collecting ideas from everyone makes people feel heard and may give choices nobody thought of.
quests.funFact: Some families write ideas on slips of paper and draw them from a bowl.

quests.instruction: A family vote ends in a tie: two for pizza and two for tacos. What can they do?
quests.correctAnswer: Talk it over or find a third choice 🤝
options: Talk it over or find a third choice 🤝
Argue loudly until somebody gives in 😠
Let the loudest person decide it all 📢
quests.hint: A tie means both ideas have support.
quests.explanation: A tie is a chance to talk, find a third choice, or take turns, like pizza today and tacos tomorrow.
quests.funFact: In many votes a tie is broken by a coin toss, though families can choose kinder ways.

quests.instruction: In the family votes, the youngest child's idea has lost every time. How can the family keep it fair?
quests.correctAnswer: Give the youngest the next pick 🌟
options: Give the youngest the next pick 🌟
Stop the youngest from voting 🚫
Count the youngest's vote as half 🔢
quests.hint: Fairness means everyone's voice counts over time.
quests.explanation: A vote sometimes does not go your way, but a fair family makes sure each person's choice is honored from time to time.
quests.funFact: Many classrooms and clubs rotate who chooses so that each person gets a turn.

quests.instruction: Ariel's family is making soup together. Which plan shares the work well?
quests.correctAnswer: Share jobs: wash, chop with help, stir 🥣
options: One person does it all while others watch 👀
Everyone chops at once without help 🔪
Share jobs: wash, chop with help, stir 🥣
quests.hint: Think about jobs that suit each helper's age.
quests.explanation: Splitting the tasks lets each person do something suitable and safe, and the soup is finished sooner.
quests.funFact: Cooking with children helps them practice measuring, counting, and following steps.

quests.instruction: Bex's family reads the recipe aloud together, one step at a time. Why does that help?
quests.correctAnswer: Everyone knows what comes next 📖
options: It makes the cooking last longer 🕰️
It means the food will taste bad 😬
Everyone knows what comes next 📖
quests.hint: A shared plan keeps everyone in step.
quests.explanation: Reading the recipe together means everyone knows the next step, so nobody adds the salt twice.
quests.funFact: In baking, the order and amounts matter because the ingredients react with each other.

quests.instruction: After the family cooks a meal together, who should help clean up?
quests.correctAnswer: Everyone shares the clean-up jobs 🧽
options: Only the person who did the cooking 🍳
Everyone shares the clean-up jobs 🧽
Nobody, it can sit until next week 🕰️
quests.hint: Teamwork covers the whole job, including the end.
quests.explanation: Cleaning up is part of the meal. When everyone shares it, the cook is not left with all the work.
quests.funFact: Many cooks say that cleaning as they go makes the final clean-up much shorter.

quests.instruction: Which of these is a real compromise?
quests.correctAnswer: They each pick one game, then swap 🎲
options: Rowan always picks and Lia agrees 😐
They each pick one game, then swap 🎲
Lia picks everything and Rowan sulks 😠
quests.hint: In a compromise, both people give something.
quests.explanation: Each person gets a turn and gives a little, so both feel respected.
quests.funFact: Compromising is a skill used by families, teams, and even countries.

quests.instruction: At the family picnic there is only one frisbee, but four children want to play. What could they do?
quests.correctAnswer: Choose a game all four can join 🥏
options: Choose a game all four can join 🥏
Fight until the strongest keeps it 💪
Hide it so that nobody plays 🙈
quests.hint: Is there a game that suits everyone at once?
quests.explanation: Looking for a game that includes everyone turns one frisbee into fun for all four.
quests.funFact: Many frisbee games can include children and adults of different abilities.

quests.instruction: Which statement about cooperation is true?
quests.correctAnswer: Everyone helps and gives a little 🤝
options: Everyone helps and gives a little 🤝
Doing everything yourself without help 🧍
Always agreeing with whatever others say 😐
quests.hint: Think about all the family situations in this level.
quests.explanation: Cooperation means working together, listening, and giving a little so that everyone gets something.
quests.funFact: Ants, bees, and many other animals cooperate to get big jobs done.
